Joe Rogan thought it had to be a conspiracy theory: AI companies quietly buying millions of books, scanning them, and throwing the originals away. Then Jamie looked it up. ROGAN: "Oh my god, it's true." Anthropic had a code name for it: "Project Panama." The internal memo: "Project Panama is our effort to destructively scan all the books in the world." "We don't want it to be known that we are working on this." Rogan's reaction: "The training data is other people's work. It's books. That's what's insane." How it played out: Anthropic bought millions of books, cut off the spines, scanned every page and discarded them. Authors sued in Bartz v. Anthropic. The judge ruled the scanning of purchased books was fair use. The pirated books were another story. Anthropic had also downloaded millions from pirate sites, and that part cost it $1.5 billion, the largest copyright settlement in US history. About $3,000 per pirated book. Interested in AI?
